strategy: Add one read-only GitHub repository-onboarding transport in front of the existing deterministic repository_onboarding_preflight. The transport queries one configured repository over HTTPS, collects only repository identity, default branch, visibility, caller permission booleans, protected-main presence, Environment names, Environment secret names, and an exact remote workspace marker. It writes a closed digest-sealed metadata artifact and exposes collect/preflight operations through root skillctl. The preflight command imports and calls the existing evaluator unchanged; it cannot start WP-08, read secret values, configure GitHub, deploy, release, merge, or set production_closed.

changes.responsibility: collect, validate, sanitize, seal, persist, and revalidate live GitHub onboarding metadata
changes.reason: no integration currently owns the live metadata input required by the existing preflight

changes.responsibility: expose bounded collect and preflight commands using one configured repository and token environment-variable reference
changes.reason: operators need one canonical process boundary rather than hand-authored JSON

changes.responsibility: prove endpoint binding, pagination, names-only secret handling, remote marker identity, sealed persistence, CLI delegation, preflight reuse, and failure behavior
changes.reason: repository admission metadata is a security and release-readiness boundary

changes.responsibility: route repository-onboarding through the canonical root control plane
changes.reason: all supported Hosts and operators must invoke the same command

changes.responsibility: document metadata endpoints, artifact contract, public-repository approval, preflight handoff, and authority exclusions
changes.reason: WP-08 operators need a precise safe onboarding procedure

unchanged_boundaries: scripts/repository_onboarding_preflight.py remains the sole repository readiness decision owner
GitHub remains the authority for repository, permission, protection, Environment, and names-only secret metadata
protected-environment-preflight remains the owner of real secret-value and endpoint validation inside the protected Job
WP-08 release coordinator remains the only owner of ReleaseRun authorization and execution
TaskRun, Quality, release, deployment, production closure, write, and merge authorities remain unchanged
customer-agent product source, services, web, contracts, and runtime dependencies remain unchanged
forbidden_repairs: Do not accept a repository, default branch, marker, permission, protection, Environment, or secret-name claim that was not returned by the configured GitHub API transport.
Do not read, request, persist, hash, echo, or validate any GitHub Environment secret value.
Do not treat a missing/forbidden API response as absence; ambiguous permission or pagination failures must fail closed.
Do not let API payloads select another repository, API origin, output path, or preflight policy.
Do not allow a public repository without the existing explicit --allow-public decision.
Do not mutate GitHub repository settings, create Environments, write secrets, dispatch WP-08, deploy, release, merge, or set production_closed.
Do not change services, web, contracts, product dependencies, or the existing onboarding evaluator.
required_invariants: all API requests are HTTPS, repository-bound, credential-redacted, and limited to read-only metadata endpoints
Environment secrets are represented only by unique names returned from the names-only listing endpoint
nonempty repository identity is derived from exact decoded remote PHASE_CANDIDATE_MANIFEST.json and release/MANIFEST.json bytes
the persisted metadata artifact has a closed schema and a canonical SHA-256 seal
reloading persisted metadata revalidates its seal and cannot broaden permissions or readiness
collect never returns PASS for onboarding and preflight delegates its decision to the existing evaluator
public repository use remains blocked unless --allow-public is explicitly supplied
every result keeps authority_effect=false, deploy_allowed=false, and production_closed=false

focused: valid private repository metadata with protected main, required Environment, secret names, and matching remote marker is sealed and passes the existing preflight
root collect and preflight commands use the same transport and deterministic evaluator
paginated Environment and secret-name responses are collected without values
counterexamples: wrong repository identity, non-main default, missing permissions/protection/Environment/secrets, malformed content encoding, marker mismatch, and seal tampering fail closed
HTTP/auth/permission/pagination ambiguity cannot be converted to a negative metadata claim
public repository remains blocked without explicit approval
regression: existing repository onboarding tests and complete skill-control-plane remain green
negative_path: no API mutation method or workflow dispatch endpoint exists
no secret value appears in durable artifacts, output, exception messages, or test evidence

risks: GitHub permission scopes may block branch-protection or Environment metadata; this must be reported as a transport block, not interpreted as missing configuration.
Public repositories require a separate explicit approval because production Environment metadata and future credentials have a different exposure profile.
GitHub contents responses are base64 encoded; exact bytes and digest must be verified before building the remote workspace marker.
A passing repository preflight is admission evidence only and does not prove production credentials, model calls, PostgreSQL, browser execution, or release closure.
rollback_plan: Remove the GitHub repository-onboarding transport, CLI route, focused tests, and architecture document; retain the existing fail-closed repository_onboarding_preflight.py metadata-input boundary and BLOCKED WP-08 state.
